zh:
第[[eight_consciousnesses|八识]]，含藏一切种子，遇缘现行；是业力[[continuity|相续]]与生命延续的载体。「阿赖耶」（ālaya）意为「藏」，具三义：能藏（能含藏诸法种子）、所藏（为诸法所熏、所依）、执藏（被末那识执为「我」）。

其运转被形容为「恒转如暴流」：刹那生灭而相续不断，非常非断。这一比喻同时回应了两种错误：执其为常（则成实体我），执其为断（则业果无所归属）。

如来藏系另有一路读法：《入楞伽经》卷7 说「阿梨耶识者名如来藏，而与无明七识共俱」——把阿赖耶识与如来藏等同，使唯识的「识」与如来藏的「心性」在后期印度与中国佛学中发生交汇。
en:
The [[eight_consciousnesses|eighth consciousness]], which contains all seeds and becomes manifest when conditions obtain; it is the vehicle of the [[continuity|continuity]] of karma and of the continuation of life. “Ālaya” means “storehouse” and has three senses: the store (neng cang, that which can contain the seeds of all dharmas), the stored (suo cang, that which is perfumed by all dharmas and is their basis), and the storehouse of appropriation (zhi cang, that which is grasped as “I” by manas).

Its operation is described as “constantly turning like a violent torrent”: it arises and perishes moment by moment yet continues without interruption, neither permanent nor annihilated. This simile answers two errors at once: taking it as permanent (which would make it a substantial self), and taking it as annihilated (which would leave the fruits of karma without an owner).

The tathāgatagarbha tradition offers another reading: the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra* (Ru Lengqie Jing), ch. 7, says, “The ālaya-consciousness is called the tathāgatagarbha, and is together with the seven consciousnesses of ignorance” — this equates ālaya-consciousness with the tathāgatagarbha, bringing the “consciousness” of Yogācāra and the “mind-nature” of the tathāgatagarbha tradition into convergence in later Indian and Chinese Buddhist thought.

sources.en: *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*, “Chapter on the Marks of Mind, Manas, and Consciousness” (Xin Yi Shi Xiang Pin)
sources.zh_q: 「一切种子心识」与「执持身」的功能说明。
sources.en_q: An account of the functions of “the mind-consciousness of all seeds” and “holding fast to the body”.

sources.zh_q: 「藏」三义；「恒转如暴流」。
sources.en_q: The three senses of “storehouse”; “constantly turning like a violent torrent”.

sources.zh_q: 「阿梨耶识者名[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]，而与无明七识共俱。」
sources.en_q: “The ālaya-consciousness is called the [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]], and is together with the seven consciousnesses of ignorance.”

zh:
大乘的核心道路：发菩提心、行[[six_paramitas|六度]]、历十地、成佛度众生。是[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]思想在大乘实践中的展开方向。

菩萨道的关键在于「菩提心」——为利益一切众生而愿成佛的志愿。这一动机把修行从「自求解脱」转为「与一切众生共同解脱」，因此大乘批评声闻乘为「自了」。

位次上，菩萨道分十地（欢喜地至法云地），配合十波罗蜜，历三大阿僧祇劫而成佛。华严、唯识、天台各有十地的详细判摄。

如来藏思想与菩萨道的连接点在于：既然一切众生本具如来藏，则「度众生」不是从无到有地给予什么，而是帮助众生除去覆盖、显发本具——这使菩萨道具有内在的必然性，而非单纯的外在命令。
en:
The core path of the Mahāyāna: arousing the mind of enlightenment, practising the [[six_paramitas|six pāramitās]], traversing the ten stages, and attaining Buddhahood in order to save sentient beings. It is the direction in which [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]] thought unfolds within Mahāyāna practice.

The key to the bodhisattva path lies in the “mind of enlightenment” (bodhicitta) — the aspiration to attain Buddhahood for the benefit of all sentient beings. This motive transforms practice from “seeking one's own liberation” into “liberation together with all sentient beings”, and on this ground the Mahāyāna criticises the śrāvaka vehicle as “self-serving”.

As to stages, the bodhisattva path comprises the ten stages (from the stage of Joy to the stage of the Dharma-cloud), coordinated with the ten pāramitās, and Buddhahood is attained after three great incalculable aeons. Huayan, Yogācāra, and Tiantai each have their own detailed assessment of the ten stages.

The point of connection between tathāgatagarbha thought and the bodhisattva path is this: since all sentient beings intrinsically possess the tathāgatagarbha, “saving sentient beings” is not the bestowal of something out of nothing but the helping of sentient beings to remove their covering and bring out what they intrinsically possess — this gives the bodhisattva path an inner necessity rather than making it a merely external command.

sources.en: *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra* (Da Bore Jing) and *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (Dapin Banruo Jing)
sources.zh_q: [[bodhisattva_path|菩萨道]]的经典基础。
sources.en_q: The scriptural foundation of the [[bodhisattva_path|bodhisattva path]].

sources.en: *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* (Huayan Jing), “Chapter on the Ten Stages” (Shi Di Pin)
sources.zh_q: 十地的详说。
sources.en_q: A detailed exposition of the ten stages.

sources.en: *Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna* (Da Cheng Qixin Lun)
sources.zh_q: 以「信成就发心」说明菩提心的发起。
sources.en_q: It explains the arousing of bodhicitta by way of “the arousing of the mind through the accomplishment of faith”.

zh:
众生本具的觉悟可能性与究竟依据。「佛性」与[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]、[[pure_mind|自性清净心]]、法性、真如、实相等概念「义一而名异」。

印度佛教的「种性」（gotra）说与中国的「佛性」说有一处重要分歧：印度瑜伽行派立「五种姓」（声闻种性、缘觉种性、菩萨种性、不定种性、无种性），主张「无种性」众生毕竟不能成佛；而《大般涅槃经》「一切众生悉有佛性」的立场，则为中国佛学「一切皆能成佛」的共识所依。

这一分歧的实践后果很大：若有无种性众生，则「普度」有一个理论边界；若一切众生悉有佛性，则菩萨道的对象是无限的。天台、华严皆取后者。
en:
The possibility of awakening and the ultimate basis that sentient beings intrinsically possess. “Buddha-nature”, [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]], [[pure_mind|the intrinsically pure mind]], the dharma-nature, suchness, and the real mark are concepts that are “one in meaning though different in name”.

There is one important divergence between the Indian Buddhist doctrine of “lineage” (gotra) and the Chinese doctrine of “Buddha-nature”: Indian Yogācāra posits the “five lineages” (the śrāvaka lineage, the pratyekabuddha lineage, the bodhisattva lineage, the indeterminate lineage, and the lineage-less), maintaining that sentient beings of the “lineage-less” kind can never attain Buddhahood; whereas the position of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* that “all sentient beings possess the Buddha-nature” became the basis for the consensus of Chinese Buddhist thought that “all can attain Buddhahood”.

This divergence has considerable practical consequences: if there are lineage-less sentient beings, then “universal salvation” has a theoretical limit; if all sentient beings possess the Buddha-nature, then the scope of the bodhisattva path is infinite. Both Tiantai and Huayan adopt the latter.

sources.zh_q: 「一切众生悉有[[buddha_nature|佛性]]」；以矿中金为喻。
sources.en_q: “All sentient beings possess the [[buddha_nature|Buddha-nature]]”; it uses gold in ore as a simile.

sources.en: *Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna* (Da Cheng Qixin Lun)
sources.zh_q: 以「一心」开[[suchness|真如]]、生灭二门，众生本具觉性。
sources.en_q: It opens the “one mind” into the two gates of [[suchness|suchness]] and of arising-and-ceasing, and holds that sentient beings intrinsically possess the nature of enlightenment.

sources.zh_q: 五种姓说，与「一切悉有[[buddha_nature|佛性]]」的立场相对。
sources.en_q: The doctrine of the five lineages, which stands opposed to the position that “all possess the [[buddha_nature|Buddha-nature]]”.

zh:
世间共许的真理。因果、善恶、修行、解脱都在这一层面上成立。

「世俗」（saṃvṛti）有「覆盖、遮蔽」与「共许、约定」两层意思：一是凡夫的认知被[[ignorance|无明]]所覆，二是世间以语言约定为实。因此世俗谛是「有效但非究竟」的：在俗谛中，杀生是恶、布施是善、因果不虚；但这一切都不成立为自性有。

[[madhyamaka|中观]]强调「不坏世俗」，正因若无俗谛则「不得第一义」——胜义不能脱离世俗的语言与因果被另外找到。
en:
The truth agreed upon by the world. Causality, good and evil, practice, and liberation all hold at this level.

“Conventional” (saṃvṛti) has the two senses of “covering, concealing” and “common consent, convention”: first, the cognition of ordinary beings is covered by [[ignorance|ignorance]]; second, the world takes linguistic convention as real. Conventional truth is therefore “valid but not ultimate”: within the conventional truth, killing is evil, giving is good, and causality is not deceptive; yet none of this holds as intrinsic existence.

[[madhyamaka|Madhyamaka]] stresses “not destroying the conventional”: precisely because without the conventional truth “the ultimate truth is not attained” — the ultimate cannot be found elsewhere, apart from the language and causality of the conventional.

sources.en: *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* (Zhong lun), fascicle 4, “Examination of the Four Noble Truths”
sources.zh_q: 青目释：「[[conventional|世俗谛]]者，一切法性空，而世间颠倒故，生虚妄法，于世间是实。」
sources.en_q: In Piṅgala's commentary (Qingmu shi): “[[conventional|Conventional truth]] means that all dharmas are empty by nature, yet because the world is inverted, illusory dharmas arise, and these are real for the world.”

zh:
眼识、耳识、鼻识、舌识、身识、意识、末那识、[[alaya|阿赖耶识]]。前六识了别粗境，末那识恒审思量，阿赖耶识持种受熏。

八识说的成立过程：前五识为感官认识；第六意识综合了别，兼缘过去未来；第七末那识（manas）恒常思量第八识为「我」，是我执的直接来源；第八阿赖耶识（ālaya）含藏一切种子，遇缘现行，承担业力[[continuity|相续]]的载体功能。

这一体系的意义在于解决「无我而轮回」的技术难题：既不需假设一个实体灵魂，又需要说明业力如何跨生命相续——阿赖耶识正是以「识的相续」而非「实体的迁移」来承担这一功能。
en:
Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness, manas, and [[alaya|ālaya-consciousness]]. The first six consciousnesses discern coarse objects, manas constantly examines and deliberates, and ālaya-consciousness retains the seeds and receives perfuming.

How the doctrine of the eight consciousnesses came to be established: the first five consciousnesses are sensory cognition; the sixth, mind-consciousness, synthesises and discerns, and also takes past and future as its objects; the seventh, manas, constantly and persistently considers the eighth consciousness as “I”, and is the direct source of self-grasping; the eighth, ālaya, contains all seeds, becomes manifest when conditions obtain, and performs the function of being the vehicle of the [[continuity|continuity]] of karma.

The significance of this system lies in solving the technical problem of “rebirth without a self”: it is necessary neither to posit a substantial soul nor to fail to explain how karma continues across lives — ālaya-consciousness performs precisely this function by way of “the continuity of consciousness” rather than “the transmigration of a substance”.

sources.en: *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*, “Chapter on the Marks of Mind, Manas, and Consciousness” (Xin Yi Shi Xiang Pin)
sources.zh_q: [[alaya|阿赖耶识]]「于身随逐、执持」的经典来源，并说「一切种子心识」。
sources.en_q: The scriptural source for [[alaya|ālaya-consciousness]] “following along with the body and holding it fast”, and for the statement “the mind-consciousness of all seeds”.

sources.zh_q: [[alaya|阿赖耶识]]的成立论证。
sources.en_q: The argument establishing [[alaya|ālaya-consciousness]].

sources.zh_q: 以十条教理成立第[[eight_consciousnesses|八识]]，并详辨末那识。
sources.en_q: It establishes the [[eight_consciousnesses|eighth consciousness]] by ten scriptural and logical proofs, and discusses manas in detail.

zh:
无自性义，而非「什么都不存在」。「空」所否定的只有一件事：自性（svabhāva）——不依他、不变、独立的存在方式。

空的表述常依[[dependent_origination|缘起]]而说。《[[doc_29|中论]]·观四谛品》的名偈：「众因缘生法，我说即是空，亦为是假名，亦名中道义。」三句分别对应：依缘起故无自性（空）、无自性而假名施设（假）、不落有无二边（中）。因此空、假、中不是三个阶段，而是同一句话的三个侧面——这也成为天台三谛说的经典依据。

空与无我的关系是直接的：空即无我，无我即空。二者所指相同，只是「空」偏重法的层面，「无我」偏重人的层面。
en:
The meaning of being without intrinsic nature, and not “nothing exists”. What “emptiness” negates is only one thing: intrinsic nature (svabhāva) — a mode of existence that is not dependent on anything else, does not change, and stands independently.

The expression of emptiness is usually given in dependence on [[dependent_origination|dependent origination]]. The famous verse of the *[[doc_29|Mūlamadhyamakakārikā]]* (Zhong lun), “Examination of the Four Noble Truths”, runs: “Whatever is dependently originated, that I call emptiness; it is also a provisional designation, and it is also called the meaning of the middle way.” The three phrases correspond respectively to: because it is dependently originated it is without intrinsic nature (emptiness); being without intrinsic nature it is provisionally designated (provisional); it falls into neither of the two extremes of existence and non-existence (middle). Emptiness, the provisional, and the middle are therefore not three stages but three facets of one and the same statement — and this too became the classical basis of the Tiantai doctrine of the three truths.

The relation between emptiness and non-self is direct: emptiness is non-self, and non-self is emptiness. The two refer to the same thing; only “emptiness” lays stress on the level of dharmas, while “non-self” lays stress on the level of persons.

sources.en: *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* (Zhong lun), fascicle 4, “Examination of the Four Noble Truths”
sources.zh_q: 「众因缘生法，我说即是空，亦为是假名，亦名中道义。」
sources.en_q: “Whatever is dependently originated, that I call emptiness; it is also a provisional designation, and it is also called the meaning of the middle way.”

sources.en: *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya Sūtra* (Heart Sutra, Bore Boluomiduo Xin Jing)
sources.zh_q: 「色即是空，空即是色；受想行识，亦复如是。」
sources.en_q: “Form is emptiness, emptiness is form; feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are likewise so.”

sources.zh_q: 空义详释，辨「众生空」与「法空」。
sources.en_q: A detailed exposition of the meaning of emptiness, distinguishing “the emptiness of sentient beings” from “the emptiness of dharmas”.

zh:
大圆镜智、平等性智、妙观察智、成所作智，由[[eight_consciousnesses|八识]]转成。

- 大圆镜智（第八识转）：如镜映万物而无分别；
- 平等性智（第七识转）：我执既断，观自他平等；
- 妙观察智（第六识转）：善观察诸法自相共相，能转法轮、断众疑；
- 成所作智（前五识转）：于一切世界示现种种变化，成办利他事业。

四智配合三身：大圆镜智与平等性智相应法身／报身，妙观察智与成所作智相应化身。这一配合使[[vijnapti_matra|唯识]]的修行论有明确的结果结构，而非仅止于「断惑」。

sources.zh_q: [[four_wisdoms|四智]]的建立与配属。
sources.en_q: The establishment and correlation of the [[four_wisdoms|four wisdoms]].

sources.zh_q: 以「[[four_wisdoms|四智]]」说明佛地功德。
sources.en_q: It explains the qualities of the stage of Buddhahood by way of the [[four_wisdoms|four wisdoms]].

zh:
《大方等[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]经》《[[doc_15|胜鬘经]]》《不增不减经》《大般涅槃经》《入楞伽经》《宝性论》等。

这一系经典的共同主题是：一切众生本具如来藏，故皆可成佛；心性本净，客尘所染。其中：
- 《大方等如来藏经》一般认为是最早出现的如来藏经典，以九喻说明众生身中有如来；
- 《胜鬘经》提出「空如来藏」与「不空如来藏」的区分，并说如来藏为「法界藏、法身藏、出世间上上藏、自性清净藏」；
- 《宝性论》以七金刚句组织如来藏义，是这一系的论书总结。

这一系经典的形成约在公元3—5世纪，晚于般若经（约前1—2世纪）而早于唯识论书的集成（4—5世纪），因此处在「空」与「识」两条主线之间——它既以空性为前提（如来藏本身即是空性的），又要为成佛提供肯定性的依据。这一位置正是中国佛学（天台、华严、禅）大量吸收它的原因。

sources.zh_q: 九喻：莲花内有化佛、淳蜜在岩树中、真金堕于不净处、弊物裹金像、贱女怀贵子等。
sources.en_q: The nine similes: a transformed Buddha within a lotus, pure honey in a rock-tree, true gold fallen into an impure place, a golden image wrapped in worthless cloth, a lowly woman bearing a noble child, and so on.

sources.en: *Śrīmālādevī Sūtra* (Shengman Jing), “Chapter on Emptiness Concealing the Real” (Kong Yi Yin Fu Zhenshi Zhang)
sources.zh_q: 空[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]与不空如来藏。
sources.en_q: The empty [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]] and the non-empty tathāgatagarbha.

sources.zh_q: [[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]与法身的关系。
sources.en_q: The relation between the [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]] and the dharma-body.

sources.en: *Ratnagotravibhāga* (Jiu Jing Yi Sheng Bao Xing Lun)
sources.zh_q: 以七金刚句组织[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]义。
sources.en_q: It organises the meaning of the [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]] by way of seven vajra points.

zh:
[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]系最具争议的两个论题，其走向决定了中国佛教的实践边界。

**一阐提**（icchantika，「欲求者」）指断尽善根、不信因果、不修梵行之人。**问题**：《[[doc_8|大般涅槃经]]》前半部主张「一阐提不能成佛」，后半部则说「一切众生悉有佛性」，一阐提亦有佛性、亦当成佛——同一部经的前后不同，正是这一争论的现场。

- **瑜伽行派（五种姓说）**——立「无种姓」，毕竟不能成佛，此说与「一阐提不成佛」相应；
- **汉传（涅槃经后分与《法华经》）**——取「一切众生悉有佛性」，判一阐提亦当成佛，成为定论；
- **竺道生**——在《涅槃经》后分尚未译出时（约5世纪初）即主张「一阐提皆得成佛」，被当时僧众判为邪说而摈出，后经文译出而印证其说，史称「孤明先发」。这是中国佛教史上**最著名的一次「以一义抗众说而最后被证实」**的案例。

**常乐我净**（四德）是对「苦、无常、无我、不净」四颠倒的反转：《涅槃经》说如来法身具常、乐、我、净四德。它对读经者是一个关键提醒——**不能把「无我、无常」当成佛教的全部结论**：在「一切众生悉有佛性」的层次上，如来藏系用的是肯定性的语汇（真常、妙有），与阿含与中观的遮诠语汇并行。两种语汇如何会通，正是汉传判教处理的核心问题。

sources.zh: 《大般涅槃经》卷7 等（前分与后分）
sources.en: *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*, fascicle 7 and elsewhere (the earlier and later parts)
sources.zh_q: [[icchantika|一阐提]]成佛问题的前后不同说法，以及常乐我净四德。
sources.en_q: The differing statements in the earlier and later parts on the question of the [[icchantika|icchantika]]'s attainment of Buddhahood, and the four virtues of permanence, bliss, self, and purity.

sources.en: *Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna* (Da Cheng Qixin Lun) and the *Buddha-nature Treatise* (Fo Xing Lun)
sources.zh_q: 以心性本净会通[[icchantika|一阐提]]亦当成佛。
sources.en_q: They harmonise, by way of the intrinsic purity of the mind-nature, the view that the [[icchantika|icchantika]] too will attain Buddhahood.

sources.zh_q: 五种姓说与无种姓的立场。
sources.en_q: The doctrine of the five lineages and the position of the lineage-less.

sources.en: *Gaoseng Zhuan* (Biographies of Eminent Monks), fascicle 7, “Biography of Zhu Daosheng” (Zhu Daosheng Zhuan)
sources.zh_q: 竺道生「孤明先发」主张[[icchantika|一阐提]]成佛而被摈的记载。
sources.en_q: The record of Zhu Daosheng's “first to illumine alone”, his maintaining that the [[icchantika|icchantika]] attains Buddhahood, and his expulsion.

zh:
一切法依因缘而生、依识而现，属[[dependent_origination|缘起]]层面。「依他」（paratantra）即「依他缘而起」——不自主、不独立，全由条件所成。

依他起是[[three_natures|三性]]中的枢纽，也是唯识与中观讨论最集中的焦点：中观认为依他起与缘起同义，即「无自性」；唯识则在承认依他起为「实有」（依他起性是有的，只是其上无遍计所执）这一点上与中观产生分歧。

在唯识系统内，依他起与「识」直接对应——依识而现，故依他起性是识所变。
en:
All dharmas arise from causes and conditions and appear in dependence on consciousness; this belongs to the level of [[dependent_origination|dependent origination]]. “Dependent on others” (paratantra) means “arising in dependence on other conditions” — not autonomous, not independent, entirely constituted by conditions.

The dependent nature is the pivot among the [[three_natures|three natures]] and also the focus of the most concentrated discussion between Yogācāra and Madhyamaka: Madhyamaka holds that the dependent nature is synonymous with dependent origination, that is, “without intrinsic nature”; Yogācāra, by contrast, diverges from Madhyamaka in acknowledging the dependent nature as “truly existent” (the dependent nature exists; it is only that the imagined nature does not exist upon it).

Within the Yogācāra system the dependent nature corresponds directly to “consciousness” — since it appears in dependence on consciousness, the dependent nature is what consciousness transforms.

sources.zh_q: 「依他起，理有情无」——依他起别有实体，非如遍计全无。
sources.en_q: “The dependent nature is existent in principle and non-existent as affection” — the dependent nature has its own distinct substantiality, unlike the imagined nature, which is wholly non-existent.

sources.zh_q: 以依他起为「分别自性」。
sources.en_q: It takes the dependent nature as “the nature of discrimination” (vikalpa-svabhāva).

zh:
把依他起的法误执为具有独立自性，属「迷」的一侧。「遍计」（parikalpa）是「周遍计度」——心于一切法上普遍地计量、执取，把它当作有自性的存在。

它的特点是「情有理无」：在众生的认识中确实存在（情有），但在实际的法上并不存在（理无）。因此它不是「又一个东西」，而是「一个错误」。

这一区分是[[vijnapti_matra|唯识]]处理「迷」的关键：迷不是多出一层世界，而是对既有世界的误读。
en:
Falsely grasping the dharmas of the dependent nature as possessing independent intrinsic nature; this is the side of “delusion”. “Imagining” (parikalpa) means “conceiving everywhere” — the mind measures and grasps universally with respect to all dharmas, taking them as existent with intrinsic nature.

Its characteristic is “existent as affection, non-existent in principle” (qing you li wu): it genuinely exists in the cognition of sentient beings (existent as affection), but it does not exist in the actual dharmas (non-existent in principle). It is therefore not “yet another thing” but “an error”.

This distinction is the key to how [[vijnapti_matra|consciousness-only]] deals with “delusion”: delusion is not an extra layer of world, but a misreading of the world that is already there.

sources.zh_q: 「遍计所执，情有理无。」
sources.en_q: “The imagined nature is existent as affection and non-existent in principle.”

sources.en: *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra* (Jie Shenmi Jing), “Chapter on the Marks of All Dharmas” (Yi Qie Fa Xiang Pin)
sources.zh_q: 遍计所执相的定义。
sources.en_q: The definition of the mark of the imagined nature.

zh:
于依他起上远离遍计所执，证二空（人空、法空）所显的[[suchness|真如]]，属「悟」的一侧。

「圆」谓圆满，「成」谓成就，「实」谓真实。它不是一个需要被制造出来的新东西，而是依他起上「去掉误执」之后所显的实际状态。因此[[vijnapti_matra|唯识]]的修行不是「获得」，而是「转舍转得」——舍掉的是遍计所执，得到的是圆成实。

圆成实即真如，即六无为中的「真如无为」，是唯识的胜义。
en:
Being free from the imagined nature on the basis of the dependent nature, and realising the [[suchness|suchness]] revealed by the two emptinesses (the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of dharmas); this is the side of “awakening”.

“Consummate” means complete, “accomplished” means achieved, “real” means true. It is not a new thing that needs to be produced, but the actual state revealed on the dependent nature once false grasping has been removed. The practice of [[vijnapti_matra|consciousness-only]] is therefore not “acquisition” but “turning away and turning toward” (zhuan she zhuan de) — what is discarded is the imagined nature, what is obtained is the perfected nature.

The perfected nature is suchness, namely the unconditioned of suchness among the six unconditioned dharmas, and it is the ultimate truth of consciousness-only.

sources.en: *Cheng Weishi Lun* (Discourse on the Perfection of Consciousness-only), chs. 8 and 9
sources.zh_q: 「二空所显圆满成就诸法实性，名圆[[chengshi|成实]]。」
sources.en_q: “The real nature of all dharmas, consummate and accomplished, revealed by the two emptinesses, is called the [[chengshi|perfected]] nature.”

zh:
心性本净，客尘所染。迷与悟因此不是获得新东西，而是去除覆盖。

「心性本净」（巴利 pabhassara-citta）的主张在阿含与部派中已有：心被客尘烦恼所染，而心的本性是清净的。部派对此有分歧——[[sarvastivada|有部]]等认为「心性本净」指的是「心未来成佛的可能性」而非「当下即净」。

到[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]系，《胜鬘经》「自性清净心，为客尘烦恼所染」成为定式。「客尘」是「客」与「尘」二喻：如客（暂住而非常住）、如尘（外来的附着物）。因此客尘即遍计所执——覆盖心性的是执取，而非心性本身。

这一结构使修行成为「去覆」而非「造作」：不需制造一个清净心，只需除去遮蔽。禅宗「明心见性」、天台「一念无明法性心」皆承此。
en:
The mind-nature is intrinsically pure, but is defiled by adventitious dust. Delusion and awakening are therefore not the acquisition of something new, but the removal of a covering.

The thesis that “the mind-nature is intrinsically pure” (Pali pabhassara-citta) already appears in the Āgamas and the schools: the mind is defiled by adventitious dust and affliction, yet the nature of the mind is pure. The schools differed on this — the [[sarvastivada|Sarvāstivāda]] and others held that “the mind-nature is intrinsically pure” refers to “the possibility that the mind will attain Buddhahood in the future” rather than to “being pure right now”.

In the [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]] tradition, the *Śrīmālādevī Sūtra*'s “the intrinsically pure mind, defiled by adventitious dust and affliction” became the standard formulation. “Adventitious dust” combines two images, “adventitious” (a temporary guest, not a permanent resident) and “dust” (an external accretion). Adventitious dust is thus the imagined nature — what covers the mind-nature is grasping, not the mind-nature itself.

This structure makes practice a matter of “removing the covering” rather than “fabricating”: there is no need to produce a pure mind, only to remove the obscuration. Chan's “illuminating the mind and seeing one's nature” and Tiantai's “a single moment of ignorance is the mind of the Dharma-nature” both inherit this.

sources.zh_q: 「[[pure_mind|自性清净心]]，为客尘烦恼所染。」
sources.en_q: “The [[pure_mind|intrinsically pure mind]] is defiled by adventitious dust and affliction.”

sources.en: *Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna* (Da Cheng Qixin Lun)
sources.zh_q: 「一心」开[[suchness|真如]]门与生灭门，觉与不觉同依一心。
sources.en_q: The “one mind” opens into the gate of [[suchness|suchness]] and the gate of arising-and-ceasing; enlightenment and non-enlightenment alike rest on the one mind.

sources.zh_q: 「[[suchness|真如]]在烦恼中，谓之如来藏；真如出烦恼，谓之法身。」
sources.en_q: “[[suchness|Suchness]] amid affliction is called the tathāgatagarbha; suchness freed from affliction is called the dharma-body.”

zh:
布施、持戒、忍辱、精进、禅定、智慧。又称六波罗蜜，「波罗蜜」（pāramitā）意为「到彼岸」——由此六者能从生死此岸到[[nirvana|涅槃]]彼岸。

六度的内在次第：布施先对治悭贪；持戒建立行为轨范；忍辱使前二者在逆境中不坏；精进使不断；禅定使心力集中；智慧则使前五者不落执著，成为「波罗蜜」而非仅是人天善法。

论书另说「三事修六度」——以「一切智智相应作意、以大悲为上首、以无所得为方便」三事配合，六度才成为[[bodhisattva_path|菩萨道]]而非仅善行。这一说明使六度与般若空慧密不可分。
en:
Giving, observance of precepts, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. Also called the six pāramitās; “pāramitā” means “gone to the other shore” — by these six one can go from this shore of birth-and-death to the other shore of [[nirvana|nirvāṇa]].

The inner sequence of the six: giving first counteracts stinginess and greed; observance of precepts establishes a norm of conduct; patience keeps the first two unbroken in adverse circumstances; diligence keeps them uninterrupted; meditative concentration concentrates the power of the mind; wisdom keeps the first five from falling into grasping, so that they become “pāramitās” and not merely human and heavenly merit.

The treatises further speak of “cultivating the six pāramitās through three matters” — only when the six are combined with the three matters of “attention concomitant with the wisdom of omniscience, great compassion as the foremost, and non-acquisition as the expedient means” do they become the [[bodhisattva_path|bodhisattva path]] rather than mere virtuous action. This account makes the six pāramitās inseparable from the emptiness-wisdom of the Prajñāpāramitā.

sources.en: *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra* (Da Bore Jing) and *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (Dapin Banruo Jing)
sources.zh_q: [[six_paramitas|六度]]的逐一详释及其相互含摄。
sources.en_q: A detailed exposition of the [[six_paramitas|six pāramitās]] one by one and their mutual inclusion.

sources.zh_q: 以「三事修[[six_paramitas|六度]]」说明六度成为波罗蜜的条件。
sources.en_q: It uses “cultivating the [[six_paramitas|six pāramitās]] through three matters” to explain the conditions under which the six become pāramitās.

sources.zh_q: 菩萨地中[[six_paramitas|六度]]的广说。
sources.en_q: An extensive exposition of the [[six_paramitas|six pāramitās]] in the Bodhisattva-bhūmi.

zh:
一切众生本具的成佛根据，即[[pure_mind|自性清净心]]、[[buddha_nature|佛性]]，只是被无明覆盖而未显现。「如来藏」（tathāgata-garbha）字面义即「如来在胎藏中」——众生身中潜在地具足如来。

它给出成佛的本体论依据，并解释迷悟的机制：心性本净，客尘所染。因此迷与悟不是「有」与「无」的差别，而是「覆」与「显」的差别。

「藏」有三义（《佛性论》卷二〈如来藏品〉）：
- 所摄藏：一切众生悉摄于如来之智内；
- 隐覆藏：法身无论因位果位俱不改变，然众生为烦恼所覆故不得见；
- 能摄藏：如来果德悉摄于凡夫心中。

本页按「成佛根据」一系的问题意识定位——即：无我既已成立，成佛的主体性依据只能落在心性本身。但这一定位并非各宗共识：中观应成派不承认实有如来藏（恐落常见），唯识也不完全等同如来藏；中国天台、华严、禅宗则大量吸收并使之成为判教核心。
en:
The basis for attaining Buddhahood that all sentient beings intrinsically possess; that is, [[pure_mind|the intrinsically pure mind]] and [[buddha_nature|Buddha-nature]], merely covered by ignorance and not yet manifest. The literal meaning of “tathāgatagarbha” (ru lai zang) is “the Tathāgata in the womb” — the Tathāgata is present in potency within the bodies of sentient beings.

It provides the ontological basis for attaining Buddhahood and explains the mechanism of delusion and awakening: the mind-nature is intrinsically pure, but is defiled by adventitious dust. Delusion and awakening are therefore not a difference between “having” and “not having” but between “covered” and “manifest”.

“Garbha” has three senses (*Buddha-nature Treatise*, Fo Xing Lun, fascicle 2, “Chapter on the Tathāgatagarbha”):
- the garbha as that which is encompassed: all sentient beings are encompassed within the wisdom of the Tathāgata;
- the garbha as concealment: the dharma-body does not change in either the causal or the fruition stage, yet sentient beings cannot see it because they are covered by affliction;
- the garbha as that which encompasses: the qualities of the Tathāgata's fruition are entirely encompassed within the minds of ordinary beings.

This page situates the concept in the line of inquiry concerned with the “basis for attaining Buddhahood” — namely: once non-self has been established, the subjective ground for Buddhahood can only fall on the mind-nature itself. This placement is not, however, the consensus of all schools: Prāsaṅgika Madhyamaka does not accept a truly existent tathāgatagarbha (for fear of falling into eternalism), and Yogācāra does not wholly equate it with the tathāgatagarbha either; Chinese Tiantai, Huayan, and Chan, by contrast, absorbed it extensively and made it central to their doctrinal classification.

sources.zh_q: 以莲花内有化佛、淳蜜在岩树中、真金堕于不净处、弊物裹金像、贱女怀贵子等九喻，说明众生身中本有如来。一般认为是最早出现的[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]经典。
sources.en_q: By nine similes — a transformed Buddha within a lotus, pure honey in a rock-tree, true gold fallen into an impure place, a golden image wrapped in worthless cloth, a lowly woman bearing a noble child, and so on — it explains that the Tathāgata is intrinsically present within the bodies of sentient beings. It is generally regarded as the earliest [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]] scripture to appear.

sources.en: *Śrīmālādevī Sūtra* (Shengman Jing), “Chapter on the Dharma-body” (Fa Shen Zhang)
sources.zh_q: 「如来法身不离烦恼藏，名[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]。」「无量烦恼藏所缠如来藏。」
sources.en_q: “The Tathāgata's dharma-body, not separate from the store of affliction, is called the [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]].” “The tathāgatagarbha enveloped by the store of immeasurable affliction.”

sources.zh_q: 以矿中金喻[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]含藏清净法身；众生悉有佛性。
sources.en_q: It uses gold in ore as a simile for the way the [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]] contains the pure dharma-body; all sentient beings possess the Buddha-nature.

sources.zh_q: 「如来之藏，是善不善因，能遍兴造一切众生。」「阿梨耶识者名[[tathagatagarbha|如来藏]]。」
sources.en_q: “The tathāgatagarbha is the cause of good and evil, and can bring forth all sentient beings universally.” “The ālaya-consciousness is called the [[tathagatagarbha|tathāgatagarbha]].”

sources.en: *Buddha-nature Treatise* (Fo Xing Lun), fascicle 2, “Chapter on the Tathāgatagarbha” (Rulai Zang Pin)
sources.zh_q: 「藏」三义：所摄藏、隐覆藏、能摄藏。
sources.en_q: The three senses of “garbha”: the garbha as that which is encompassed, the garbha as concealment, and the garbha as that which encompasses.

zh:
空、无相、无愿（又译无作）。是趣入解脱的三种观门，与[[two_truths|二谛]]、[[three_natures|三性]]密切相关。

- 空门：观一切法无我、无我所，诸法虚幻不实；
- 无相门：因空故不著于相，离一切相；
- 无愿门：因无相故于三界生死无所爱染愿求。

论书有两个关键区分：一是「三三昧」通有漏无漏，而「三解脱门」唯通无漏——《俱舍论》卷28：「此三各二种，谓净及无漏……于中无漏者名三解脱门，能与涅槃为入门故。」二是瑜伽行派以三性建立三门——《瑜伽师地论》卷74 以遍计所执立空解脱门、依他起立无愿解脱门、圆成实立无相解脱门。

《大智度论》卷20 则以「涅槃城有三门」为喻，并说：「是三解脱门，摩诃衍中是一法，以行因缘故，说有三种」——三种门实为一法，因众生根机（爱多者、见多者、爱见等者）不同而开为三。

来源上要注意：「三解脱门」这一名称并未出现在巴利四部尼柯耶中，属较后出的定型；见于竺法护译《佛说力士移山经》、僧伽提婆译《增壹阿含》8.3经、施护译《佛说法印经》，并与《杂阿含经》第80经、《佛说圣法印经》相当——后者正是三法印得名的可能来源。
en:
Emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (also rendered as non-activity, wu zuo). These are three contemplative doors entering into liberation, closely related to the [[two_truths|two truths]] and the [[three_natures|three natures]].

- The door of emptiness: contemplating all dharmas as without self and without anything belonging to a self, all dharmas being illusory and unreal;
- The door of signlessness: because of emptiness, not attaching to signs, free from all signs;
- The door of wishlessness: because of signlessness, having no craving or aspiration with respect to birth-and-death in the three realms.

The treatises make two key distinctions. First, the “three samādhis” extend to both defiled and undefiled, whereas the “three doors of liberation” are exclusively undefiled — *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya* (Jushe lun), ch. 28: “Each of these three is of two kinds, pure and undefiled … among them the undefiled ones are called the three doors of liberation, because they can serve as the entrance to nirvāṇa.” Second, the Yogācāra school establishes the three doors by way of the three natures — *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* (Yoga Shidi Lun), ch. 74, establishes the door of liberation of emptiness by the imagined nature, the door of liberation of wishlessness by the dependent nature, and the door of liberation of signlessness by the perfected nature.

*Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* (Da Zhidu Lun), ch. 20, uses the image that “the city of nirvāṇa has three gates”, and says: “These three doors of liberation are one dharma in the Mahāyāna; because of the cause of practice they are spoken of as three kinds” — the three doors are in fact one dharma, opened into three according to the differing faculties of sentient beings (those with much craving, those with much view, those with craving and view equally).

As to provenance it should be noted that the name “three doors of liberation” does not occur in the four Pali Nikāyas; it is a later fixed formulation. It occurs in Dharmarakṣa's translation *Fo Shuo Lishi Yi Shan Jing*, in Saṅghadeva's translation of the *Ekottara-āgama* (Zeng Yi Ahan), sūtra 8.3, and in Dānapāla's *Fo Shuo Fayin Jing*, and corresponds to sūtra 80 of the *Saṃyukta-āgama* (Za Ahan Jing) and to the *Fo Shuo Sheng Fayin Jing* — the latter being precisely the possible source of the name “three seals of the Dharma”.

sources.zh_q: 透过空、无相、无所有三种禅观，最后观[[anatta|无我]]我所而离慢习、得知见清净，名为「圣法印」。
sources.en_q: Through the three contemplations of emptiness, signlessness, and nothingness, one finally contemplates [[anatta|non-self]] and what belongs to a self, thereby abandoning the habit of conceit and attaining purity of knowledge and vision; this is called the “seal of the noble Dharma”.

sources.zh_q: 「于中无漏者名[[three_doors|三解脱门]]，能与涅槃为入门故。」
sources.en_q: “Among them the undefiled ones are called the [[three_doors|three doors of liberation]], because they can serve as the entrance to nirvāṇa.”

sources.zh_q: 「诸法实相是[[nirvana|涅槃]]城，城有三门：空、无相、无作。」「摩诃衍中是一法，以行因缘故说有三种。」
sources.en_q: “The real mark of all dharmas is the city of [[nirvana|nirvāṇa]], and the city has three gates: emptiness, signlessness, and non-activity.” “In the Mahāyāna it is one dharma; because of the cause of practice it is spoken of as three kinds.”

sources.zh_q: 「三种解脱门亦由三自性而得建立。」
sources.en_q: “The three doors of liberation are likewise established by way of the three natures.”

zh:
[[vijnapti_matra|唯识]]学的迷悟结构：[[parikalpita|遍计所执性]]、依他起性、圆成实性。三者不是三个世界，而是对同一缘起法的三种认识状态。

三者的关系是：
- 依他起——一切法依因缘而生、依识而现，是存在的实际层面；
- 遍计所执——在依他起法上误执有独立自性，属「迷」；
- 圆成实——在依他起上远离遍计所执，证二空所显真如，属「悟」。

因此三性中「依他起」是枢纽：迷与悟都不离它，差别只在是否在其上起了执。与二谛的对应是：遍计所执属假有，依他起属世俗有，圆成实属胜义有。

三性也是三解脱门的建立依据（见《瑜伽师地论》卷74），因此这一组概念同时贯通了唯识的存有论、认识论与实践论。
en:
The structure of delusion and awakening in [[vijnapti_matra|consciousness-only]] (Yogācāra): the [[parikalpita|imagined nature]], the dependent nature, and the perfected nature. The three are not three worlds but three cognitive states with respect to one and the same dependently originated dharmas.

Their relation is as follows:
- The dependent nature — all dharmas arise from causes and conditions and appear in dependence on consciousness; this is the actual level of existence;
- The imagined nature — falsely grasping the dharmas of the dependent nature as possessing independent intrinsic nature; this belongs to “delusion”;
- The perfected nature — on the basis of the dependent nature, being free from the imagined nature and realising the suchness revealed by the two emptinesses; this belongs to “awakening”.

Hence within the three natures the dependent nature is the pivot: neither delusion nor awakening is apart from it, the difference lying only in whether grasping has arisen upon it. The correspondence with the two truths is: the imagined nature is provisional existence, the dependent nature is conventional existence, the perfected nature is ultimate existence.

The three natures are also the basis on which the three doors of liberation are established (see *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, ch. 74); this group of concepts therefore runs through Yogācāra ontology, epistemology, and soteriology at once.

sources.en: *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra* (Jie Shenmi Jing), “Chapter on the Marks of All Dharmas” (Yi Qie Fa Xiang Pin)
sources.zh_q: 以「遍计所执相、依他起相、圆[[chengshi|成实]]相」建立三相，是此说的经典来源。
sources.en_q: It establishes the three marks as “the mark of the imagined nature, the mark of the dependent nature, and the mark of the [[chengshi|perfected]] nature”; this is the scriptural source of the doctrine.

sources.en: *Cheng Weishi Lun* (Discourse on the Perfection of Consciousness-only), chs. 8 and 9

zh:
转依的核心：转舍杂染、转得清净。「转识成智」即[[eight_consciousnesses|八识]]转为[[four_wisdoms|四智]]，是唯识学的究竟目标。

「转依」（āśraya-parāvṛtti）的「依」指所依——阿赖耶识及一切种。转依不是说心的实体发生变化，而是说识的「所依」从杂染转为清净：第八识转成大圆镜智、第七识转成平等性智、第六识转成妙观察智、前五识转成成所作智。

关键在「转」字：不是消灭识、另成一个智，而是同一功能在舍离执著后的转变。这与中观「烦恼即菩提」、天台「一念无明法性心」在结构上相通，但唯识保留了更详细的位次与机制说明。
en:
The core of “transformation of the basis”: turning away from the defiled and turning toward the pure. “Transformation of consciousness into wisdom” means that the [[eight_consciousnesses|eight consciousnesses]] are transformed into the [[four_wisdoms|four wisdoms]]; it is the ultimate goal of Yogācāra.

In “transformation of the basis” (āśraya-parāvṛtti) the “basis” (āśraya) means that which is relied upon — ālaya-consciousness and all its seeds. Transformation of the basis does not mean that the substance of the mind changes, but that the “basis” of consciousness turns from defiled to pure: the eighth consciousness becomes the great mirror wisdom, the seventh becomes the wisdom of equality, the sixth becomes the wisdom of wondrous observation, and the first five become the wisdom of accomplishing what is to be done.

The key lies in the word “transformation”: it is not the annihilation of consciousness and the creation of another wisdom, but the transformation of the same function once grasping has been relinquished. This is structurally akin to Madhyamaka's “afflictions are themselves enlightenment” and Tiantai's “a single moment of ignorance is the mind of the Dharma-nature”, though Yogācāra preserves a more detailed account of the stages and the mechanism.

sources.zh_q: [[eight_consciousnesses|八识]]转四智的次第与配属。
sources.en_q: The sequence and correlation by which the [[eight_consciousnesses|eight consciousnesses]] are transformed into the four wisdoms.

sources.zh_q: 转依（āśraya-parāvṛtti）的系统论释。
sources.en_q: A systematic exposition of transformation of the basis (āśraya-parāvṛtti).

zh:
[[conventional|世俗谛]]与[[ultimate|胜义谛]]。作用是：既不坏世间因果，又不执究竟实有，从而同时避免常见与断见两种极端。

「谛」（satya）是「真实」义，但二谛的「真实」方式不同：世俗谛是「于世间为实」——世间颠倒故生虚妄法，而此法于世间是实；胜义谛是「于圣者为实」——圣者真知颠倒性故，知一切法皆空无生。因此二谛不是两个世界，而是同一批法的两种认识层次。

各派解释差异较大：
- 说一切有部：以「法」（实有）与「假名」（施设有）区分；
- 中观：《中论·观四谛品》「诸佛依二谛，为众生说法，一以世俗谛，二第一义谛」——二谛属言教层次，三论宗更以「于谛／教谛」明言二谛「唯是教门，不关境理」；
- 唯识：世俗为识所现，胜义为二空所显真如。

二谛的实践意义在于：不坏世俗而证胜义，故既能持戒、修行、承担伦理责任，又不把任何一法执为究竟。
en:
[[conventional|conventional truth]] and [[ultimate|ultimate truth]]. Their function is neither to destroy worldly causality nor to cling to any ultimate substantial reality, thereby avoiding at once the two extremes of eternalism and annihilationism.

“Truth” (satya) means “real”, but the two truths are “real” in different ways: conventional truth is “real for the world” — because the world is inverted, illusory dharmas arise, and these dharmas are real for the world; ultimate truth is “real for the noble ones” — because the noble ones truly know the nature of inversion, they know that all dharmas are empty and unborn. The two truths are therefore not two worlds but two levels of cognition with respect to one and the same set of dharmas.

Interpretations differ considerably among the schools:
- Sarvāstivāda: distinguishes “dharmas” (substantially real) from “provisional designations” (prajñapti-sat);
- Madhyamaka: the *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* (Zhong lun), “Examination of the Four Noble Truths”: “The Buddhas teach the Dharma in reliance on the two truths: one the conventional truth, the other the ultimate truth” — the two truths belong to the level of verbal teaching, and the Sanlun school goes further, using “the truth for [the world] / the truth as teaching” to state explicitly that the two truths “are only a teaching device, and have nothing to do with the object or the principle”;
- Yogācāra: the conventional is what consciousness manifests, the ultimate is suchness revealed by the two emptinesses.

The practical significance of the two truths is this: without destroying the conventional one realises the ultimate, and so one can observe the precepts, practise, and bear ethical responsibility, while clinging to no single dharma as ultimate.

sources.en: *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* (Zhong lun), fascicle 4, “Examination of the Four Noble Truths”
sources.zh_q: 「诸佛依[[two_truths|二谛]]，为众生说法：一以世俗谛，二第一义谛。若人不能知，分别于二谛，则于深佛法，不知真实义。」
sources.en_q: “The Buddhas teach the Dharma to sentient beings in reliance on [[two_truths|the two truths]]: one is the conventional truth, the other the ultimate truth. Those who cannot understand this distinction between the two truths do not know the true meaning of the profound Buddha-Dharma.”

sources.en: *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* (Zhong lun), fascicle 4, “Examination of the Four Noble Truths”
sources.zh_q: 「若不依俗谛，不得第一义；不得第一义，则不得[[nirvana|涅槃]]。」
sources.en_q: “Without relying on the conventional truth, the ultimate truth is not attained; not attaining the ultimate truth, [[nirvana|nirvāṇa]] is not attained.”

sources.zh_q: 「诸佛说法，常依俗谛、第一义谛，是二皆实，非妄语也。」
sources.en_q: “The Buddhas' teaching always relies on the conventional truth and the ultimate truth; both are true, and it is no falsehood.”

sources.zh_q: 「佛法中有[[two_truths|二谛]]：一者世谛，二者第一义谛。」
sources.en_q: “In the Buddha-Dharma there are [[two_truths|two truths]]: one is the conventional truth, the other the ultimate truth.”

zh:
究竟真理：一切法空、无自性、不可得。

「胜义」（paramārtha）是「最殊胜的境义」，指圣者智慧所对的境。它的内容不是「另一个更真实的实体」，而是「一切法无自性」这一事实本身。

因此胜义谛不可被正面表述——凡说出的都已是世俗的言说。这就是《[[doc_29|中论]]》以「八不」遮诠的原因，也是「实相不可说」与「三藏十二部」之间表面的张力所在（后者恰是以言说指月的必要方便）。
en:
The ultimate truth: all dharmas are empty, without intrinsic nature, ungraspable.

“Ultimate” (paramārtha) is “the most excellent object of meaning”, referring to the object of the noble ones' wisdom. Its content is not “another, more real entity” but the fact itself that “all dharmas are without intrinsic nature”.

Ultimate truth therefore cannot be expressed positively — whatever is spoken is already conventional speech. This is why the *[[doc_29|Mūlamadhyamakakārikā]]* (Zhong lun) uses the “eight negations” in a via negativa, and it is also where the apparent tension lies between “the real mark cannot be spoken” and “the three baskets and twelve divisions” (the latter being precisely the necessary expedient of pointing at the moon with words).

sources.en: *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* (Zhong lun), fascicle 4, “Examination of the Four Noble Truths”
sources.zh_q: 青目释：「诸圣贤真知颠倒性故，知一切法皆空无生，于圣人是第一义谛，名为实。」
sources.en_q: In Piṅgala's commentary: “Because the noble sages truly know the nature of inversion, they know that all dharmas are empty and unborn; for the noble ones this is the ultimate truth, and it is called real.”
